newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends lower on large US crop, technicals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends lower on large US crop, technicals.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on spillover from Tuesday's USDA forecast for 1997 U.S. wheat production which was well above expectations and on a technical slide, traders said.
"There are too many longs in the market and the technical signs are starting to roll out and turn bearish," said Warren King, analyst for Cargill Investor Services.

The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) for the September Friday reached overbought status at 70 percent and at Thursday's close stood at 47 percent, a near neutral number which gives the market more room for volatility.
The market views an RSI of 70 percent or more as overbought and 30 percent or less as oversold.
CBOT soft red winter wheat closed 4-1/2 to seven cents lower, with September down six at $3.55-1/4 a bushel.
Although U.S. export sales remain strong, the large supply of wheat in the U.S. diminished concerns about wheat end-users having difficulty originating their mill and export needs.

USDA in its August crop report Tuesday said 1997 U.S. wheat production totalled 2.531 billion bushels, above the government's July forecast for 2.431 billion and above an average of analysts' estimates for 2.476 billion.
Further, USDA Tuesday pegged 1997-98 foreign ending stocks of wheat at 105.57 million tonnes, above the government's estimate in July for 102.37 million tonnes.
A drop in soybean futures also was cited as a pressuring factor for the CBOT wheat futures market, pit traders said.
Losses were limited by USDA's weekly export sales data that came in above trade expectation and by news Jordan had purchased 50,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat.
USDA Thursday said during the week ended August 7 U.S. net export sales of wheat totalled 641,700 tonnes, above expectations for 400,000 to 500,000 tonnes.
But the large supply of wheat negated the perceived supportive influence of the export sales numbers.
"Export sales are good, very good but this is a big crop," Cargill's King said. Also "the spread actions say the market doesn't need wheat right now."
Term Commodities bought four million bushels of December, SAK Futures and Refco Inc each sold two million bushels of December, traders said.
In spread dealings, Tenco Inc did one million bushels of September/December at 15-1/2 cents, premium December, sources said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 22,000 contracts, below the 26,313 traded Wednesday.

In wheat options, Paine Webber bought 150 December $3.60 puts at 11 cents and sold 150 December $3.50 puts at 7-1/2 cents, traders said. Dean Witter sold 150 December $3.70 puts at 14-1/2 cents and ABN Amro, The Chicago Corp bought 150 December $4.00 calls at eight to nine cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated by the CBOT at 4,000 contracts, below the 4,238 traded Wednesday.
